data.name: Arnavansh
data.gender_notes: Arnavansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arna means 'eternal' and Ansh means 'creation' or 'descendants'. This name is derived from the Sanskrit language and holds deep roots in Hindu mythology. The name Arnavansh carries the meaning “Eternal creation, descendants” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arnavansh usually hope their child will grow to embody eternal creation, descendants and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of eternal creation and legacy.
data.etymology: Arnavansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Eternal creation, descendants.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arnavansh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Arnavansh conveys a sense of timelessness and continuity in Hindu culture. It is a reminder of the cyclical nature of life, where our actions and creations live on beyond us, shaping the world for generations to come. This name is often given to children as a blessing for a prosperous and flourishing future.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Arnavansh represents the eternal soul, which is constantly reborn and evolves over many lifetimes. The name serves as a reminder to live in the present moment and make every action count towards growth and spiritual progress. It is a name that inspires a deep sense of duty, responsibility, and connection to one's heritage and ancestors.

historical_references.reference: Arnavansh was an esteemed title given to the rulers of the Chandela dynasty in Central India during the 10th and 11th centuries CE.
Arnavansh is also mentioned in the Sanskrit epic Mahabharata, as an ancestor of Bhishma Pitamaha, a central character in the epic.
